jacqueline-mars.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
jacqueline-mars.period: Estate-tax campaign in the 1990s–2000s; report published April 2006
jacqueline-mars.summary: Historical estate-tax research implicates family-company advocacy, but does not establish Jacqueline’s individual direction or return.
jacqueline-mars.mechanism: Family-company resources → estate-tax advocacy; individual direction unresolved

support.text: Public Citizen and United for a Fair Economy identify Jacqueline among the Mars siblings and describe company-funded efforts to repeal estate tax. The authors advocate retaining the tax.
support.source: Public Citizen / United for a Fair Economy, report p. 36

counter.text: The report’s projected tax savings are conditional estimates, not money shown to have been received by Jacqueline. Its spending evidence is predominantly company- and family-level.
counter.source: Public Citizen / UFE: attribution and estimate limits

counter.text: Mars currently says it discloses lobbying but makes no corporate candidate or party contributions. That company policy does not establish Jacqueline’s personal giving or disprove historical lobbying.

jacqueline-mars.limitations: No numerical estimate: the source identifies an economically relevant lobbying mechanism without assigning Jacqueline individual control of it. Historical corporate roles, inheritance and projected tax savings are not enough to fill every person-level dimension. The underlying lobbying filings were not independently reconstructed.

john-mars.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
john-mars.period: Estate-tax campaign in the 1990s–2000s; report published April 2006
john-mars.summary: John’s family-company political activity is documented; his personal decisions and resulting gains remain unresolved.
john-mars.mechanism: Family-company estate-tax lobbying; person-level control and realized return unresolved

support.text: The report identifies John among the siblings with senior corporate roles and describes payments by Mars Inc. to an estate-tax lobbying group. It does not itemize his personal instructions.
support.source: Public Citizen / United for a Fair Economy, report p. 36

counter.text: Company payments are not automatically John’s personal payments. The report’s estimated family benefit is contingent on repeal, not a demonstrated individual windfall.
Mars distinguishes disclosed lobbying from corporate campaign contributions, which its policy prohibits. Neither statement amounts to a record of John’s individual political activity.

john-mars.limitations: No numerical estimate. Family-level research is retained as evidence to investigate, not transferred wholesale to John. More direct evidence of his decisions and policy outcomes is required; lack of a score is not a clean bill of health.

giovanni-ferrero.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
giovanni-ferrero.period: European lobbying declarations through 2026; governance announcement, March 2026
giovanni-ferrero.summary: Ferrero International’s policy access is visible in a lobbying-record compilation. Giovanni’s strategic leadership is separately documented, but those facts do not establish that he attended the meetings or obtained a personal preferential decision.
giovanni-ferrero.mechanism: Corporate policy access and strategic control; individual action and outcome unresolved

support.text: Ferrero’s March 2026 announcement identifies Giovanni as president of its holding company, with new leadership roles reporting to him and a continuing group strategy remit.

MEP of the Week compiles Ferrero International’s declared meetings on issues including deforestation and packaging. It is an independent aggregation of disclosure records, not evidence Giovanni personally attended.
support.source: MEP of the Week: Ferrero International record

counter.text: Ferrero’s published business-conduct code prohibits bribes and political-party or candidate contributions. A stated rule is not independent evidence of compliance, nor does it rule out lawful lobbying.
counter.source: Ferrero: Code of Business Conduct, p. 5

giovanni-ferrero.limitations: No score: a corporate meeting log does not establish an individual favor or reciprocal bargain. The EU register page did not expose usable record text during this review, so the compilation is explicitly secondary. Private tax arrangements and business leadership alone do not establish oligarchy.

paolo-ardoino.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
paolo-ardoino.period: Volcano Energy announcement, June 2023; licensing and headquarters move, January 2025
paolo-ardoino.summary: Ardoino publicly links Tether’s investment and relocation to El Salvador’s crypto strategy. The record supports a commercial-policy partnership, but the reviewed licensing and tax framework is broader than Tether and does not establish a bespoke political favor.
paolo-ardoino.mechanism: Executive-led investment and jurisdiction choice ↔ public crypto strategy and sector incentives

support.text: Tether’s January 2025 announcement quotes CEO Ardoino explaining its planned relocation after obtaining a digital-asset license and presents the move as aligned with El Salvador’s policy direction.
Tether’s June 2023 announcement quotes then-CTO Ardoino supporting its participation in Volcano Energy. The project’s billion-dollar ambition is not a statement that Tether alone paid that amount.
Reuters describes a public-private mining project with a government revenue participation and Tether among initial investors; Tether’s contribution was not specified.
support.access: Indexed Reuters article passage reviewed; direct retrieval unavailable

support.text: The US International Trade Administration describes tax exemptions for registered issuers, certifiers and service providers, alongside licensing, fees and regulatory oversight.

counter.text: The tax framework applies to defined classes of registered participants, not just Tether. The same account describes the regulator’s power to suspend or cancel registrations.
counter.source: US International Trade Administration: scope and safeguards

paolo-ardoino.limitations: Historical, episode-limited estimate of a policy partnership, not corruption. It does not establish that Ardoino wrote the law, personally received all company benefits, or paid for a license. Investment announcements are not completed-spending audits. Other executives’ alleged political channels are not assigned to him.

rationales: A personally articulated executive role in investments aligned with a public policy project.
A registered business can benefit from broad sector incentives; a bespoke personal favor is not established.
Investment, a state-linked project and a policy-aligned relocation form a specific but non-exclusive commercial-policy relationship.
